reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that traditional sports analytics operate on Run 1 of Pearl’s ladder—associational inference—which fails under adversarial conditions. Observational models like those based on nflfastR or Bayesian ratings misinterpret correlation as causation, leading to Simpson’s paradox and confounded regime shifts. For instance, a team trailing may pass more frequently, but this does not imply poor strategy—it reflects a response to adverse conditions. The true causal effect P(\text{Win} \mid \text{do}(\text{PassRate} = p)) must be estimated through intervention rather than mere observation. This necessitates a Structural Causal Model (SCM) where variables are linked via directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), allowing for graph mutilation and do-calculus operations. The GSE engine uses such SCMs to simulate shocks like "do(Inactive=LeftTackle)" and compute their downstream impacts. Meanwhile, GSI integrates these causal estimates into conformal prediction frameworks to maintain calibrated uncertainty bounds despite non-iid data streams. The failure mode arises when models assume exchangeability or ignore latent variables, causing performance degradation under real-world volatility.
